intro_html: Smothered pork chops are Southern for a reason: golden fried chops buried under onion gravy with cream stirred in. Every bowl packs 45 grams of protein over rice for about $2.32. Sunday dinner comfort at a Tuesday leftover price.
cost_closing_html: About $2.32 a bowl for fried pork chops smothered in creamy onion gravy over rice. A soul food plate like this runs $15 at a restaurant, and they will not send you home with 13 more.
shop_smart: Pork chops carry this batch at about $21.88. Family packs and bone-in sales are your friend, anything under $4 a pound is a green light to stock the freezer.
The flour, oil, broth, and rice are all pantry players. One bag or bottle covers several batches, so the real cash outlay for this recipe is mostly just the meat.
Heavy cream is the one small splurge at about $2.58. Buy the pint, use what the gravy needs, and the rest makes your weekend coffee feel expensive.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Season the pork chops with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne, then dredge them in the flour. Save the leftover seasoned flour, that is your gravy starter.
Fry the chops in vegetable oil over medium-high heat, about 4 minutes per side, until golden and 145F inside. Work in batches and set them on a plate.
Pour off all but a few tablespoons of the oil, then cook the onions in the drippings until soft and browned at the edges. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in a few spoonfuls of the reserved seasoned flour and cook 1 to 2 minutes, then whisk in the chicken broth slowly so it stays smooth. Simmer until it thickens into gravy.
Stir in the heavy cream, return the chops, and let them smother in the gravy for 10 minutes on low.
Serve the chops and gravy over the rice.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Portion rice, chop, and gravy to that number and each bowl lands at about 896 calories with 45 grams of protein. This one is a heavyweight, built for big days.
upsell_html: Hearty dinners for about $2.32 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

steps: Cook the rice and set aside.
Season pork chops, dredge in flour, and fry to golden and 145F, then remove.
Cook onions and garlic in the drippings, stir in reserved seasoned flour, then whisk in broth to make gravy.
Stir in heavy cream, return the chops, and simmer 10 minutes.
Serve chops and gravy over rice and portion into 14 containers.
